Copying the account into the project would create the exact duplicate-truth problem 2B's authored block was built to remove.

changeRequests.change: Consider giving the CONTENT lineage hashRef an exclusion set the way template got one — at minimum `report`, and decide whether `slot-accounting.json` belongs there too.
changeRequests.why: The content stage artifact is hashed with NO exclusions. content:qa already wrote report/ into a content run dir before Task 27; Task 27 widens that surface (report/telemetry.jsonl, and revalidateSlotValues refreshes slot-accounting.json on every content:validate). Running content QA/validate against a release project's lineage content run therefore drifts the content stage hash. Unlike template this is NOT a hard refusal — content is an executable stage, so drift degrades to stale + a rerun — which is why I did not change it as an integration seam. Recorded, not fixed.

limitations: The new accounting log line in contentStageRunner is NOT asserted by any check. smoke:release passes `log: () => {}` to buildRelease, so the text never appears in the suite output. What IS proven is that the statement executes without throwing: smoke:release 27.22/27.24 drive the real (non-stubbed) contentStageRunner through a full build, and an absent `accounting` field would have raised a TypeError on the very next line.

I ran only the nine suites the brief names plus typecheck. The remaining eight of the 17 suites (playwright, verifier, selector, multi-observer, interaction-detector/explorer/patterns, sitespec, reconstruction, reconstruction-qa, e2e) were NOT run — that is the orchestrator's full-regression job, per the brief.
